title: Hammerly
description: An app designed for my fiance and I to keep track of our renovation projects in our new house, with a login function, it is an updated version that sets itself apart from it predecessor with a database migrated onto Supabase and published by Vercel, and of course made in VSCode with React and Redux toolkit

title: Hammershøj
description: The first iteration of the Hammerly app, in .NET coded in C# with a SQL database, using Entity Framework for database management and Razor Pages for the frontend. The page isnt set up for https so you might get a security warning, but I can assure you its safe to proceed.

title: ParkWhere
description: A web application for checking wether a parking lot is full, using a REST Api to fetch data and update available space from a SQL database, and displaying it in a user-friendly interface. Using a Raspberry pi with a camera and Ultrasound Sensor we can look up a license plate through a thirdparty API and add said car to our database and show it in a UX friendly way.

title: Movie App
description: A simple movie app built with React, using the TMDB API to fetch movie data and display it in a user-friendly interface. The app allows users to sort movies by popularity, release date, and rating. A fun little excercise to get familiar with React and API integration.

title: Zeaway
description: A C# based app, which uses Entity FrameWork with an SQL database to withhold information of users and cars. The whole idea is that people need to be able to drive together to school to be more viable, users are able to create their own cars and create trips, which other users are able to join
